summary: Burst-induced GPU context-switching causing serialization, p95 regressions and intermittent 429/504s in customer's dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: NimbleDocs (dedicated pool) reported a sharp degradation in throughput during short bursts of traffic on 2026-03-10 morning. Symptoms include elevated p95/p99 latency, serialization of requests to 1-2 GPUs, and intermittent 429/504 responses. No functional errors in model outputs were reported, but customer-facing requests timed out or received throttling responses.

Impact: Production traffic for critical features saw 20-40% request failures during 5-10 minute bursts across their reserved pool. Customer is on a committed dedicated contract; business impact is high.

Initial timeline: 2026-03-10 09:18 UTC - first alert (p95 > 1.4s). 09:24 UTC - increased 429 rate. 09:30-09:40 UTC - customer reports user-facing errors. 10:05 UTC - ticket opened with support.

Observed behaviour: During bursts, device metrics showed frequent CUDA context initialization events, high kernel setup time, and repeated eviction of model KV cache entries. Autoscaler logs show multiple scale-downs followed by rapid scale-ups within short windows. Hypothesis: mis-sized autoscale min_replicas+aggressive scale-down policy is causing model reinitialization and cache repopulation on GPUs, which serializes work and amplifies noisy-neighbor effects when background batch jobs overlap with user inference.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure a dedicated pool with min_replicas=1 and aggressive scale-down (30s) and enable background batch jobs on the same pool.
2) Send a sustained low-rate traffic baseline (50 rps) and then inject a burst (500 rps) for 2-5 minutes.
3) Observe p95 and 429/504 rates in console and check GPU metrics (context init, kernel setup times).
4) Repeat with min_replicas=2 and observe reduced serialization.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 11:00 UTC - Pulled device metrics: elevated CUDA_CTX_INIT count during bursts; NV driver reports increased context switch activity.
2026-03-10 11:20 UTC - Autoscaler events show scale-down followed by two scale-ups within 90s repeatedly during burst windows.

2026-03-10 11:45 UTC - KV cache eviction correlated with high mem-pressure from background batch jobs scheduled on same pool. Hot-models repopulate cache causing device-to-device transfers and kernel reinitialization.
2026-03-10 12:10 UTC - Reproduced locally by forcing autoscaler to min_replicas=1 and running a synthetic embedding-heavy workload. Observed identical p95 spikes and serialization.

2026-03-10 13:00 UTC - Hypothesis refined: aggressive scale-down + shared batch jobs create a timing window where hot models are reloaded on limited GPUs, producing head-of-line serialization and exposing noisy-neighbor GPU contention.
2026-03-11 09:30 UTC - SRE tested mitigation: set min_replicas=2 and disabled background batch on pool; immediate drop in p95 and removal of 429s during burst tests.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Engineering requested traces and NV driver logs for deeper root-cause analysis; assigned to runtime/allocator owners.
comments: Aisha Raman (Support): 2026-03-10 10:12 - Logged initial ticket and requested full GPU metrics and autoscaler history from customer.
NimbleDocs (Customer): 2026-03-10 10:23 - Confirmed burst pattern and noted background nightly batch window overlaps with morning integration tests.
Marco Li (SRE): 2026-03-10 11:05 - Observed kernel setup spikes; suspect repeated model reinit. Will try raising min_replicas as a quick mitigation.
Priya Shah (Runtime Eng): 2026-03-11 14:40 - Looking into allocator behavior during KV eviction; shared batch jobs may be causing memory thrash leading to device-to-host paging in rare cases.
Marco Li (SRE): 2026-03-11 09:35 - Applied temporary mitigation (min_replicas=2, disabled batch jobs on pool) and requested customer to validate.
resolution: Mitigation applied: increased min_replicas from 1 to 2, disabled background batch jobs on the dedicated pool, and applied a temporary hold on aggressive scale-down policy. Customer reports normalized p95 and no further 429s during repeated burst tests. Engineering to run deeper root cause analysis (allocator/kernel) and propose a durable fix (better eviction policy + autoscaler hysteresis).
resolution_notes: Temporary fix reduced customer impact. Next steps: runtime team to instrument finer-grained KV cache metrics, scheduler to add autoscaler hysteresis flag for dedicated pools, and capacity planning to recommend min_replicas baseline for bursty workloads. Planned follow-up: schedule patch and release notes, customer onboarding doc update around batch-job isolation. Target ETA for durable fix: 2026-04-02.
